scenes.heading: Variables

scenes.heading: recursion
scenes.caption: Recursion is a function that solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller version of the same problem, until it hits a base case that stops. It matches problems that contain smaller copies of themselves, such as folders inside folders, or a list you handle one item at a time.

scenes.heading: Inheritance
scenes.caption: Inheritance lets a new class start from an existing class and then add or replace behaviour. The new class is the child. The existing one is the parent. It is useful when several types really are the same kind of thing with a twist. It is harmful when you use it only to reuse a few lines.

The existing one is the parent

scenes.heading: Step by step: Inheritance
scenes.caption: Name what is truly shared. That belongs on the parent. Put only the difference on the child. Call the parent's setup so the child is fully initialised. If the “is a kind of” sentence sounds fake, do not inherit. Compose instead.

scenes.heading: Polymorphism
scenes.caption: Polymorphism means you can call the same action on different types, and each type does the version that is right for it. The caller does not have to know the exact type. It is how you write one loop that draws shapes, charges payments, or saves records, while each kind of thing keeps its own details.

scenes.heading: Step by step: Polymorphism
scenes.caption: Agree on the action name and what it promises. Give each type its own body for that action. Hold the items in a collection typed as the shared idea. Call the action in a loop. Each item runs its own body.

items: Agree on the action name and what it promises.
Give each type its own body for that action.
Hold the items in a collection typed as the shared idea.
Call the action in a loop. Each item runs its own body.

scenes.heading: Queue
scenes.caption: A queue is a collection where the first item in is the first item out. New work joins the back. You serve the front. It is the honest model for jobs, messages, and people waiting. Cutting to the front is a bug, not a feature.

items: A queue is a collection where the first item in is the first item out
New work joins the back
You serve the front

scenes.heading: Step by step: Queue
scenes.caption: Enqueue at the back. Dequeue from the front. Look at the length before you dequeue. Do not use a stack if fairness of order matters.

scenes.heading: Mocking
scenes.caption: Mocking replaces a collaborator, such as a payment service, with a stand-in you control. The test decides what the stand-in returns. It lets you test your logic without calling the real service. It lies if the stand-in drifts away from the real service.

items: Mocking replaces a collaborator, such as a payment service, with a stand-in you control
The test decides what the stand-in returns

scenes.heading: Step by step: Mocking
scenes.caption: Mock at the edge, not inside the function you are testing. Make the stand-in return the case you care about: success, and then one failure. Do not assert the mock was “called” as your only check. Assert the outcome.

items: Mock at the edge, not inside the function you are testing.

scenes.heading: The other hours today

scenes.heading: stack
scenes.caption: A stack is a collection where the last item you put in is the first item you take out. Push adds. Pop removes the most recent. Function calls, undo buttons, and matching brackets are all stacks. The most recent open thing closes first.

items: A stack is a collection where the last item you put in is the first item you take out
Push adds
Pop removes the most recent
Function calls, undo buttons, and matching brackets are all stacks. The most recent open thing closes first

scenes.heading: Step by step: stack
scenes.caption: Push items as you open them. Pop when you close the most recent one. Peek if you need to look without removing. Popping an empty stack is an error. Guard it.

items: Push items as you open them.
Pop when you close the most recent one.
Peek if you need to look without removing.
Popping an empty stack is an error. Guard it.
